Let \(D_p=(d(A,B)^p)_{A,B\in X}\). Since \(X=\binom{[6]}3\) is an \(S_6\)-set, \(\mathbb R^X\) splits into four Johnson eigenspaces of dimensions
\[
1,\ 5,\ 9,\ 5.
\]
On the three nonconstant pieces, the eigenvalues of \(D_p\) are
\[
\mu_1=3-3\cdot 2^p-3^p,\qquad
\mu_2=3^p-2^p-1,\qquad
\mu_3=-3+3\cdot 2^p-3^p.
\]
Thus \(p\)-negative type holds exactly while all three are \(\le 0\). For \(0<p\le1\), subadditivity gives \(3^p\le 1+2^p\), so \(\mu_2\le0\), and one checks \(3^p-3\cdot 2^p+3\ge0\), so \(\mu_3\le0\). At \(p=1\),
\[
\mu_2=\mu_3=0,\qquad \mu_1=-6<0.
\]
For every \(p>1\), strict superadditivity gives \(3^p>1+2^p\), so \(\mu_2>0\). Hence
\[
\wp=1.
\]

At \(p=1\), the zero eigenspace is the direct sum of the \(9\)- and \(5\)-dimensional eigenspaces, so
\[
\dim E=14.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
E=\left\{c:\sum_{A\ni i}c_A=0\text{ for every }i\in[6]\right\},
\]
the kernel of the \(6\times20\) incidence matrix of points versus triples.

For a support \(S\subseteq X\), a \(4\)-dimensional subspace supported in \(S\) exists iff the incidence matrix restricted to \(S\) has nullity at least \(4\). If \(|S|\le7\), then the corresponding \(0/1\) weight-\(3\) vectors lie in an affine space of dimension at most \(2\), but any affine \(t\)-space contains at most \(2^t\) Boolean vertices. Thus \(|S|\le4\), contradiction. Hence \(d_4\ge8\).

Equality is attained exactly as follows: partition \([6]\) into three unordered pairs, and take the \(8\) triples obtained by choosing one element from each pair. These \(8\) triples form a \(3\)-dimensional affine cube inside the hypersimplex, so their incidence rank is \(4\), giving nullity \(8-4=4\). Conversely, any support of size \(8\) with nullity \(4\) must be such a cube. The number of such partitions is
\[
\frac{6!}{2^3\,3!}=15.
\]
Each support gives exactly one \(4\)-dimensional subspace, its full kernel.

Therefore
\[
\boxed{(1,14,8,15)}.
\]
